features.text: The patient is 58 years old and male.
The patient injured his right knee a week ago at a trampoline park.
The patient experiences pain on the outside of his right knee.
The pain is sharp when pressure is applied to the right knee.
The patient has noticed bruising on his right knee.
The patient experiences instability in his right knee when walking.
The patient has been limping due to the right knee injury.
The patient has no prior knee injuries, surgeries, or conditions such as arthritis or ligament tears.
The injury occurred when the patient heard a snap and felt a sudden sharp pain in his right knee while jumping on a trampoline.
The patient believes he may have twisted his knee or landed awkwardly on the trampoline.
The patient can bend his right knee slightly but finds it uncomfortable.
The patient can straighten his right knee but finds it uncomfortable.
The patient experiences a feeling of instability in his right knee, especially when walking.
The patient has not had any imaging studies done for his right knee injury yet.
The patient has not received the results of the X-ray for his right knee injury yet.
The patient has not experienced any locking or clicking in his right knee since the injury.
The patient has not noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in his leg.
The patient has not undergone any previous imaging or diagnostic tests for knee injuries.
The X-ray results have been reviewed and showed no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
The patient has not had an MRI yet and does not have the results for that.
The patient is waiting for the doctor to review the X-ray results and provide findings.
